sentence_stem: Had the committee been better informed,
correct_completion: the proposal would have been rejected outright.
full_sentence: Had the committee been better informed, the proposal would have been rejected outright.
acceptable_variants: the proposal would never have passed.
the members would have voted against it immediately.

options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a real result of something that actually happened. The stem describes an imagined past condition, so a real result does not fit.

options.text: the proposal is being rejected now.
options.why_wrong: The present continuous describes an ongoing action. It does not complete an inverted third conditional, which needs 'would have' plus a past participle.

options.text: the proposal would have been rejected outright.
the proposal will be rejected outright.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' expresses a future prediction. An imagined past condition requires 'would have' plus a past participle.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: Had the committee been better informed is an inverted third conditional, with the if-clause written without 'if'. The main clause must use would have plus a past participle to express the imagined past result.
